_comment: M9.1 (docs/plans/GLOBAL-PLAN.md) — AutoMod rules THIS REPO manages for the Game On Portugal
guild, reconciled by `bun run:command automod:apply --apply`.
DELIBERATELY EMPTY. The guild is already moderated, and not from here.
Checked against the live guild (818108848492773377) on 2026-08-20, there are five enabled
AutoMod rules, all created by hand in the Discord UI by a moderator:
1. 'Custom Keyword Rule'          keyword   — 1 keyword; block + alert + 60s timeout
2. 'Commonly Flagged Words'       preset    — Discord presets 1,2,3 (profanity, sexual
content, slurs); block + alert
3. 'Block Spam Content'           spam      — block + alert
4. 'Block Mention Spam'           mentions  — block + timeout + alert
5. 'Sharing links - non verified' keyword   — 7 keywords, 3 exempt roles; block + alert
That is a real, curated moderation policy — including exempt roles someone thought about —
and it is better than anything invented from outside the community. So it stays where it is,
owned by the moderators who wrote it, and this file does not attempt to mirror it.
Importing those five rules here would be actively worse: it would create a second source of
truth for the same policy, and it would bring them under this reconciler's management, so a
later `--apply` would silently revert whatever a moderator had since changed in the UI. A
config file that fights the people using the product is not configuration, it is a trap.
Nothing here can touch those rules. Reconciliation only ever reads, writes or deletes rules
whose name carries the `[gop-managed:<key>]` marker (Domain/Moderation/ManagedName.ts); none
of the five names match, so they are invisible to the plan — including under
`--prune-orphaned`. AutoModPlan.test.ts pins that as a property.
The old bot's `specialchannels` table — the equivalent of `commandsOnlyChannels` below — held
0 rows in production, so there is nothing to port forward there either.
WHEN TO ADD SOMETHING HERE: when a rule needs to be reviewable in git, or applied identically
to more than one guild, or changed as part of a code change. Day-to-day moderation tweaks
belong in the Discord UI, where a moderator can make them without a deploy. Add a rule with a
`key`, set `enabled`, and run `automod:apply` (dry-run by default) to see the diff first.
